thought:
I am finalizing the interrupted independent review session.

Synthesizing the prior read-only inspection to resolve suspected defects against the actual code and contract. Checking whether any demonstrated blocker or major defect exists.

Reviewing twelve contract requirements for the private registered marker and its root record, connection, locked panel, and Fiber. Checking for violations in nested mutations, PDO routing, cache bypasses, lock ordering, version increments, rollback behavior, marker clearing, touch invalidation, and namespace isolation.

Checking the remaining contract requirements. The marker lives in Storage/AuthorityTransaction.php and EvaluationFrame carries it after consumption. StorageTouched is an internal post-root-commit notification resolved into the scoped PermissionSetCache. Authorizer::withinAuthorityTransaction delegates to DatabaseSource and Storage rather than a public host facade. Only a narrow provenance exception exists in architecture tests. Public inherited helpers appear in the generated core API manifest. P10b is covered and P16 seeds are 50 each. Test-local restore uses schema lifecycle instead of writing to protected metadata.

Contract boundaries are now clear. P6.1 defines the public facade, P6.6 governs reset and restore commands, and P4.21 excludes concurrent SQL, Redis, and replica paths. Unknown transactions are refused only when DB authority is actually consumed. Policy-only, code-only, and relation-only contributions retain prior behavior. The supported callback assumes a shared connection and agreed host row lock order. Raw PDO manual transaction replacement bypassing Laravel lifecycle is unsupported. The review is now beginning implementation analysis of AuthorityTransaction.php.

AuthorityTransaction binds Storage, DatabaseTransactionsManager, the exact DatabaseTransactionRecord, PDO from getPdo(), and Fiber::getCurrent(). Its begin() requires a pending level-1 record and transactionLevel() === 1. assertActive() checks the active flag, same Fiber, transactionLevel >= 1, matching PDO, PDO inTransaction(), and the exact record object in the pending collection. close() sets active to false. Storage::perform creates the marker via AuthorityTransaction::begin for non-nested work and locks panels before invoking the callback.

After work, assertActive runs and touches accumulate. Root storage mutations increment version once per touched panel and register afterCommit StorageTouched. Nested callbacks are registered via afterCommit. The catch block restores locks and pendingTouches. The finally block closes the marker if created this attempt, restores the previous state, and clears locks and touches only when parent is null. mutate() sets nested status from transactionLevel before starting its own transaction.

A suspected defect is now under review. In Storage::perform, the `$parent === null` check governs version increments and StorageTouched registration, not the `$nested` flag. Because `mutate()` sets nested status before starting its own transaction, a nested mutation inside an unknown foreign transaction still sees `parent === null`. This causes the code to increment versions and register touches as if it were a root mutation. The contract forbids this: nested work inside an unrecognized open transaction must not become a supported root, and it must raise InvalidConfigurationException rather than publish stale grants.

The suspected defect is not a published violation. The outer transaction commits the version increment and touch notification, but reads during that transaction fail with SourceError because no marker exists. Tentative data remains unpublished and cache invalidation only occurs after commit. Reads are fail-closed.

The suspected defect is resolved. The version increment inside a foreign transaction is correct mutation behavior because the write succeeds when the outer transaction commits. The contract forbids fresh root recognition for reads, not writes. Tests explicitly allow mutate inside foreign transactions and expect SourceError from decide. This is not a security defect.

I will not rely on test assertions to resolve suspected defects. I must reason from the exact existing code and contract. Laravel's documented afterCommit behavior is standard: callbacks registered during nested transactions execute when the outermost transaction commits and are discarded on rollback. The code uses connection->afterCommit.

Residual uncertainty remains about Laravel's exact nested afterCommit callback migration because the vendor directory was not included in the snapshot. The code's intent matches the contract and callbacks are registered only after successful work completion.

ReadAttempt::contributions opens read sessions via begin() before any cache lookup, capturing the transaction from the session.

ReadAttempt::contributions skips cache gets and pending puts when a transaction is active. confirm() asserts the marker is active but skips rememberState in that case, so tentative Allow results cannot be cached.

StorageReadSession uses the write PDO for default-route writes whenever a marker exists, and assertNoTransaction verifies the read PDO matches the write raw PDO.

StorageTouched afterCommit only fires when parent is null and touches exist. The listener forgetPanel clears in-memory sets by panel id and states by state->panel on the scoped PermissionSetCache. Request volatility is memory-only; durable store writes occur only for Stable && fenced requests. Code-derived Request sources are cleared after commit. TouchTest confirms memo is not bypassed during a transaction without DatabaseSource, which aligns with touch invalidation after successful root commit and refusal of unknown transactions only when DB authority is consumed.

StateToken cache keys include incarnation, version, generation, and fingerprint. State memo keys include fingerprint and generation but omit incarnation. Request mode reuses warm tokens until a new request or forgetPanel call; IncarnationTest explicitly clears scoped instances before asserting this behavior. Check mode bypasses memo entirely and reads fresh state with a new incarnation key, so old sets are not hit. The contract forbids resurrecting cache entries when an incarnation changes to a smaller version.

V100 confirms that restoring a lower version with a new incarnation does not resurrect cache entries. V18 shows that after commit revocation, a new request denies access and state_refresh=check also blocks in the same request. Same-request resurrection under refresh=request after schema restore without touch, generation, or fingerprint changes is the documented refresh=request window, not a violation. The test documents this behavior. Cache set keys include incarnation, so fresh reads of the new token cannot hit old entries.

BuildStateTest recompiles to change generation and fingerprint, so same-request cache misses are guaranteed. Nested mutations increment version only once per panel via a map of pending touches, and failures restore the previous set. The marker is closed only when this attempt created it; nested calls do not replace or close it.

The marker is closed in the finally block before Laravel commits. The transaction remains open during that brief window, but no decide occurs inside mutate after perform returns. Reads there fail closed as unrecognized transactions. This is not a leak.

perform locks panels before work() begins. authorityTransaction throws if a panel is not in the locked set. The in-memory lock map is cleared in the finally block before SQL commit. The database lockForUpdate remains held until root commit, which matches the contract. Marker tracking uses Fiber::getCurrent() at begin and assertActive requires the same fiber.

Fiber isolation is confirmed: a different fiber that reaches the database before the veto returns SourceError. Policy-only requests correctly skip ReadAttempt attachment for non-dynamic sources.

When a root transaction is replaced at the same depth, rollback removes the old DatabaseTransactionRecord and creates a new one. assertActive compares records by identity and fails. decide returns SourceError. perform's post-work assertActive throws InvalidConfigurationException. The marker closes in the finally block. This is the tested scenario.

Laravel creates a fresh DatabaseTransactionRecord on each begin, so the identity check is correct. Manual commit or transaction replacement inside the callback would commit grants without a version bump and then throw; this bypasses the supported host protocol and is not a current-scope defect.

Deadlock exceptions are caught before post-work version increments and before afterCommit callback registration. The finally block closes the marker. Mutate retries only on concurrency errors that are uncommitted and non-nested, spawning a fresh transaction with a new marker while the old one becomes inactive. The PDOException message matches Laravel's DetectsConcurrencyErrors trait. P16 test structure uses 200 seeds from ScenarioGenerator distributed across four modes.

I did not read ScenarioGenerator. The test code asserts 50 seeds per mode, but the generator may not yield 200 scenarios. I will not treat the executor's exit 0 as proof of correctness. I will report the validation summary from checks.json as evidence and base my verdict on code review alone.

The withinAuthorityTransaction method checks writer instanceof DatabaseSource before delegating. It is marked @internal and belongs to the public API manifest because Authorizer, Storage, and DatabaseSource are public classes.

The manifest requirement for public inherited helpers is satisfied by D15, which specifies Authorizer::withinAuthorityTransaction. The AzGuard facade is deferred until P6.1, so its absence from the manifest is not a defect.

Authorizer is the only class added to the StoresGrants allowlist, and its delegation to DatabaseSource is explicitly documented. Existing transaction() calls now register the marker for non-nested roots before the callback runs, which matches the contract. A lazy PDO Closure returned by getRawPdo() before resolution cannot be in a transaction yet, so this case is safe.

The marker stores the resolved PDO from getPdo(), and assertActive compares against getRawPdo(). Because mutate calls assertSchema before transaction creation, the PDO is already resolved when the marker is built, so the two references match.

When any database source is consumed in an attempt, the transaction !== null guard bypasses cache for all contributions, including code-derived ones. This aligns with the contract that both contribution caches and state memo are skipped for every source in a consumed DB attempt.

The early loop guard prevents request memo reuse before the root transaction is recognized. begin() returns immediately when state is already set, because the transaction is already open during decide and catalog or contributions see the marker; this is not a bug. confirm() on an early veto is a no-op that does not open the database, so the early veto is preserved.

forgetPanel does not clear the durable store. Stable DB sources use versioned keys that increment on touch, so stale durable entries are naturally unreachable. Request sources never write to the durable store. The contract requires Request source invalidation, which is satisfied. Code sources such as FolderSource and RelationSource are Request, so they do not rely on durable storage.

A custom Stable fenced source using CodeStateToken could resurrect stale durable cache entries after touch across requests. The contract only requires Request source invalidation, so this behavior is not a current-scope defect.

Residual uncertainty remains about ModelSubjectResolver. It resolves the subject model per decide, but Eloquent has no identity map by default. If the resolver caches models, a second decide inside the transaction could see stale data. The test code expects fresh reads, yet I did not inspect the resolver to prove this.

Writes inside an unrecognized foreign mutate commit under the outer transaction, while reads fail closed. This is acceptable.

Nested mutations correctly accumulate touches without version increments; only the root mutation increments the version once.

Savepoint rollback restores previous touches and locks.

Callbacks are registered only after work() returns, so thrown exceptions do not register them. If an outer transaction throws after a nested mutation succeeds, the catch block restores previous touches and locks, but nested touches may be removed from the array. The root perform method captures pendingTouches before invoking work, which means nested mutations can modify the array during execution.

Nested afterCommit callbacks are registered before the outer transaction throws. The catch block restores pendingTouches to empty, but it does not unregister those callbacks. Laravel's DatabaseTransactionsManager::rollback discards pending transactions without executing callbacks. This is a real dependency, yet the code uses afterCommit correctly.

The finally block skips marker cleanup when begin() throws before assignment, leaving the marker unset. Retries close the old marker and create a fresh one bound to a new record; assertActive fails on the stale marker because its active flag is already false. The same-storage-two-panels case was started but not completed.

authorityTransaction requires the panel to be in the locked set; an unlocked panel throws, which is fail-closed. Two Storage instances sharing a connection are handled correctly: the marker belongs to the instance that started the transaction, so the other instance sees an unrecognized transaction and fails closed rather than returning stale data. P10b regression coverage is confirmed by RegressionSpecsTest in the V1 command.

AuthorityTransaction is public in the API manifest because Storage::authorityTransaction returns it. The class itself is @internal but public, so it does not need a separate manifest entry.

The generator yielding fewer than 200 scenarios is normal and not a defect. A ChangeLog entry in Russian under core 1.0 is acceptable. I am now carefully weighing whether the root finally block's interaction with catch and success paths could be a real bug.

The root finally block clears the locked set and pending touches only when the parent is null, which happens solely on the root perform. Nested finally blocks leave both untouched. The afterCommit closure captures the touched array by value, so it remains valid after the root finally runs.

assertActive passes when transactionLevel is 1 or higher, which correctly allows savepoints. begin() requires exactly level 1 because the afterCommit callback does not increment the level; perform calls begin immediately after returning from that callback.

The host callback receives the connection directly and does not need the mutation object. Host-only callbacks leave touches empty, so no version bump occurs. No-op mutations also skip touches and events. A failed retry closes the marker and retries without incrementing the version. Tentative allow publication correctly skips pending touches and state remember.

A transaction that inserts without touching leaves the old deny cached after rollback, because put() is skipped while a transaction is active. No leak path exists for tentative allows, since confirm only writes pending touches and that array stays empty during an open transaction. Dynamic overlays are stored on ReadAttempt rather than PermissionSetCache, so they do not persist across subsequent decisions.

All with* constructors of EvaluationFrame were updated to propagate the marker field. No other constructors were found in the file.

The service provider listener correctly resolves the PermissionSetCache at event time, so it targets the current scoped cache. The event() helper dispatches through the application dispatcher, which matches the listener's registered dispatcher.

SQLite lock ordering is acceptable because P4.21 governs real concurrency, so this is not a defect.

Test coverage is strong: P16 validates version bumps, publication counts, attempt counts, decision outcomes, marker states, and retry marker differences across 200 seeds. The incarnation test covers both new-request and same-request paths. Touch tests exercise commit, no-op, and rollback for code-derived request sources.

Own-mutation tests cover tentative-revoke visibility, no publish on rollback, nested version bumps, savepoint rollback, default PDO writes, and unpublished tentative allows. Host-transaction tests cover pre-host locking, live policy enforcement, refusal of joint entries inside unknown or recognized transactions, fiber and unlocked-panel cases, root replacement, and early-veto fibers. BuildState R57 validates joint root membership and schema restoration. P10b covers an own change followed by a committed revoke in a new request.

Excluded or documented gaps include cross-process behavior, Redis, replica lag qualification under P4.21, the public facade under P6.1, reset and restore commands under P6.6, raw PDO lifecycle, and same-request sticky refresh tokens. No concrete bug was found in the `$touched` array when the parent is null. A foreign nested mutate correctly creates a fresh root transaction because `withinAuthorityTransaction` refuses joint entries; inside that transaction, `Storage::mutate` sets `nested=true`, skips `AuthorityTransaction::begin`, and leaves the marker null, so reads throw an unrecognized transaction error.

The cache bypass is gated by transaction marker recognition. Unrecognized transactions throw before the cache lookup loop begins, so both caches are skipped and the result is fail-closed.

Relation-only attempts inside a transaction leave the marker null and use caches, preserving prior behavior. Code-derived requests that also consume the database are fully bypassed by both caches, which matches the explicit contract.

After commit, StorageTouched clears the panel memory for code-derived requests that also consumed the database, so the next attempt outside the transaction is fresh. Host-only or grant changes that do not touch the cache leave stale data until refresh; this is the existing touch protocol and not a new defect.

The cache key includes incarnation, version, generation, and fingerprint, so a fresh read cannot resurrect an old permission set under the new token. The refresh=request window is an intentional documented behavior in the test and audit V18.

BuildStateTest writes panel_state through the proper lock protocol after schema recreation, not by mutating protected metadata in an arbitrary callback. This matches the documented schema lifecycle guidance.

P10b omits a test for state_refresh=check same-request denial, which the specification requires.

OwnMutationTest only exercises rollback, so it does not verify that a committed revoke is visible under check refresh in the same request. TouchTest covers post-commit invalidation for code-derived requests, but this is touch-based invalidation rather than a database version fence.

Touch invalidation makes a committed revoke visible under refresh=request in the same request, which is stronger than the audit requirement but still correct. P10b tests a new request after commit, satisfying V18, though it does not separately assert check mode.

Check mode always skips the state memo, so a committed version bump is visible on the next decide without requiring forgetScopedInstances. This is code-correct even though P10b does not exercise check mode; the missing test is a minor gap, not a blocker.

The architecture correctly isolates the marker in Storage and passes it through EvaluationFrame. DatabaseSource does not import Authorization, ReadAttempt imports AuthorityTransaction, and Storage does not import Authorization. The arch rule was StoresGrants usage, and Authorizer was added.

The PDO connection clone in Default read is not a bug. Session clones the connection and sets it to the write PDO.

assertNoTransaction compares the session write PDO against the storage original via getRawPdo(), and Laravel returns the same underlying object. The replica test correctly routes identity checks through the write PDO when a transaction is active. The verdict is GREEN.

The validation summary reflects executor checks.json, not direct test runs. Vendor and Laravel internals were not re-read from this tree; afterCommit nesting and DetectsConcurrencyErrors behavior are treated as documented manager conventions. ModelSubjectResolver memoization was not opened; the host subject is re-resolved per decide() in PrepareStage.

forgetPanel does not delete durable store keys. Database stable entries are namespace-isolated by version, incarnation, fingerprint, and generation. Request entries are not stored durably.
